longTitle.officialTitle: To designate the Rocksprings Station of the U.S. Border Patrol located on West Main Street in Rocksprings, Texas, as the “Donna M. Doss Border Patrol Station”.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “Donna M. Doss Memorial Act of 2021”.

paragraph.chapeau: A native of the State of Washington, Agent Donna Marie Doss—

subparagraph.content: proudly and honorably served her country as an Agent of the U.S. Border Patrol for more than 15 years;
began her service with the U.S. Border Patrol in 2003; and
graduated as part of the 569th Session of the Border Patrol Academy with Class 584 on June 6, 2005.
served on a Drug Enforcement Administration Task Force on the southern border for 3 years before being assigned to the northern border;
was promoted to Supervisory Border Patrol Agent in Laredo Border Patrol Sector, where she was named an Operations Officer in 2016; and
relocated to Abilene, Texas in 2017, where she served as a Resident Agent.

paragraph.content: On February 2, 2019, Agent Doss responded to a call for assistance from the Texas Department of Public Safety near Interstate 20 in Tye, Texas. While on scene, Agent Doss was struck and killed by a passing vehicle.
Agent Doss is survived by her husband, father, mother, 2 stepchildren, a sister and a brother.

section.heading: DESIGNATION.
section.content: The Rocksprings station of the U.S. Border Patrol located on West Main Street in Rocksprings, Texas, shall be known and designated as the “Donna M. Doss Border Patrol Station”.

section.heading: REFERENCES.
section.content: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the station described in section 3 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Donna M. Doss Border Patrol Station”.
